vision_features.image_context: Close-up photograph of a single broad leaf, likely from a leguminous plant (possibly soybean), showing the upper surface. The leaf is roughly oval-shaped with a prominent central midrib and visible secondary veins. A partial second leaf is visible at the top-left corner. A green stem is partially visible at the right edge.
vision_features.abnormalities: Multiple small marks are distributed across the mid and lower-central portions of the leaf surface, concentrated between the midrib and the leaf margins. Each mark follows a similar pattern: a central dark body (dark reddish-brown to nearly black-purple) that is roughly circular to slightly irregular in shape, approximately 1–4 mm in diameter. Surrounding each dark central spot is a pale yellow-green to light yellow halo, roughly 3–8 mm in overall diameter, creating a distinct two-tone appearance. The larger marks (up to ~4 mm central dark area) are found more toward the left-center of the leaf near the midrib, while smaller marks (1–2 mm dark center) are scattered more broadly across the leaf. The dark centers appear slightly dry and slightly sunken compared to surrounding tissue. The yellow haloes are diffuse and blend gradually back into the normal green tissue. No raised or powdery surface structures are visible on the upper surface. Distribution is scattered but somewhat clustered in the mid-leaf zone, with fewer marks toward the leaf tip and base. Approximately 20–30 individual marks are visible across the leaf surface.
vision_features.absences: 1. No powdery or dusty coating is visible on the leaf surface. 2. No thread-like or fuzzy growth is present on or around any of the marks. 3. No water-soaked or greasy-looking tissue is apparent around the marks. 4. No tiny raised pustules, dots, or exudate are visible within or around the dark centers on the upper surface.
vision_features.summary: The leaf displays numerous small, scattered marks distributed across its upper surface, each consisting of a dark reddish-brown to near-black circular center (1–4 mm) surrounded by a distinct pale yellow-to-yellow-green halo (3–8 mm overall). The marks are most concentrated in the mid-leaf zone between the midrib and margins. The leaf is most severely affected in its central region. The most striking feature is the strong two-tone contrast between the very dark, dry central spots and their bright yellow-green surrounding halos against the otherwise healthy dark-green leaf tissue.

Available classes in 'Soybean_Diseases' (5 total):
   1. Bacterial_Blight
   2. Diaporthe
   3. Green_stem_disorder
   4. Phomopsis
   5. Phytophthora

Knowledge-base entry for 'Bacterial_Blight':
────────────────────────────────────────
Infections begin as small, angular, water-soaked spots that turn yellow and then brown as the tissue dies. Lesions have dark reddish-brown centers surrounded by yellowish-green halos around water-soaked tissue; lesions may coalesce to form large, irregularly shaped lesions. Leaf veins may become affected creating necrotic areas resembling lightning on the leaf. Eventually lesions fall out leaving ragged foliage.. Presence of a yellowish-green halo around lesions; most common on young leaves in mid to upper canopy whereas brown spot is usually seen on older, lower leaves; lack of fungal structures in lesions.. Septoria brown spot, brown spot
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Diaporthe':
────────────────────────────────────────
Parallel rows of black, flask-shaped specks or pycnidia on mature soybean stems occurring later in the season (R6 to R8 growth stages). Pycnidia may also develop on dry, poorly developed pods, but may be dispersed randomly rather than arranged linearly.. Parallel rows of black, flask-shaped pycnidia arranged linearly on stems; random dispersal on pods.
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Phomopsis':
────────────────────────────────────────
Infected seed are cracked, shriveled, dull, and may have a gray mold on them.. Seed infected by pod and stem blight may decompose after harvest and have low viability; seedlings grown from infected seeds may often be blighted.
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Green_stem_disorder':
────────────────────────────────────────
All or part of the soybean plant remains green while the rest of the plant or neighboring plants mature, most commonly seen in stems, leaves or pods; stems remain moist while pods and seeds have ripened.. Stems and occasionally leaves remain green and moist after pods and seeds have ripened and turned brown; excessive leaves on plant and green stems when neighboring plants are near harvest maturity.
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Phytophthora':
────────────────────────────────────────
Young plants show rapid yellowing and wilting with soft rot and collapse of the root. Mature plants exhibit general yellowing of lower leaves progressing upward, followed by wilting and death, with brown discolored roots and a dark chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending from below the soil line upward several nodes; leaves typically stay attached after plant death.. The best diagnostic symptom on susceptible varieties is a lower stem discoloration (dark chocolate-brown) that may extend several nodes up the stem. Root system shows lateral and branch roots almost completely discolored; tap roots with brown surface discoloration and tan to brown inner tissue discoloration. Leaves turn yellow, wilt, and typically stay attached after plant death.. stem canker, Pythium
────────────────────────────────────────

DISCRIMINATING: 'Bacterial_Blight' vs 'Phytophthora'
Ruling feature : Presence of leaf lesions with halos (Disease A) vs. dark chocolate-brown stem/root discoloration from soil line upward (Disease B)
Bacterial_Blight: Angular, water-soaked leaf spots with dark reddish-brown centers surrounded by yellowish-green halos; lesions may coalesce and fall out leaving ragged foliage, with vein necrosis resembling lightning patterns.
Phytophthora: Dark chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending from below the soil line upward several nodes, accompanied by brown/discolored roots and yellowing leaves that remain attached after plant death.
Decision rule  : IF the primary symptom is angular leaf lesions with yellowish-green halos and no significant stem/root discoloration, THEN diagnose Bacterial Blight (Disease A); IF the primary symptom is dark chocolate-brown stem discoloration at the soil line extending upward with root rot and wilting without distinctive leaf lesions, THEN diagnose Phytophthora (Disease B).
